claim_checks.claim: TLS-oriented model for 401 rivers, 13 production zones, 2014–2016: farm egg output per biomass varies up to 8.1× (zones 3 vs 13); Pearson r=0.70 with local biomass density (p=0.008).
claim_checks.extract_quote: The estimated production of salmon louse eggs per mean standing stock of farmed salmonids (Eggs per bio.; Table 1) varied by a factor of 1.22/ 0.15 = 8.1 and was significantly correlated to LBD (Pearson r = 0.70, df = 11, p = 0.008).

claim_checks.claim: Sentinel-cage calibration (N=7911 fish, 329 trials): log(IP) coefficient 0.843 (p<0.001), theta=2.733, ICC=0.551; explains ~39% log-scale variation (adj. R²).
claim_checks.extract_quote: The random effect in the mixed model gave an intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC, (Dohoo et al., 2003)) equal to 0.551. The mixed effect negative binomial dispersion parameter theta was estimated to 2.733, yielding quantiles of the distribution of lice numbers as in Fig. 6.

claim_checks.claim: Highest expected lice loads and mortality in production zone 3 (west); zone 6 second-highest proportional mortality 2016 despite lower per-river infestation than zone 3.
claim_checks.extract_quote: The estimated proportional louse-induced mortality was highest in production zone 3, with the basic scenario varying from 2–17% and the worst case scenario varying between 10–72%, between rivers in 2016.

claim_checks.claim: 2016 basic scenario river mortality ~2–17% (zone 3), worst-case ~10–72%; overall higher risk in 2016 than 2014–2015; progression 8.2 cm s⁻¹, 20 g smolts, Taranger et al. (2015) mortality steps.
claim_checks.extract_quote: The estimated proportional louse-induced mortality was highest in production zone 3, with the basic scenario varying from 2–17% and the worst case scenario varying between 10–72%, between rivers in 2016.
